outlook.body:
- Improve operational efficiency, increase the share of value-added products and deepen engagement with high-value applications
- Make the Kharagpur brownfield expansion central to the forward agenda - not only adding tonnage but enhancing readiness for the next phase of demand and enabling faster response and more specialised applications
- Strengthen the capital base and financial flexibility through a proposed Rights Issue of up to Rs. 45 crore to support long-term growth plans
- Modernise the manufacturing ecosystem through technology - implementation of SAP HANA during the year, plus better monitoring, improved inspection systems and stronger process controls
- Sustain globally accepted quality certifications as a differentiator that enables the Company to serve demanding customer applications
- Build market presence in key end-use sectors, deepening engagement with customers in automotive, power, defence and aerospace-related segments, supported by participation in industry forums and exhibitions including Alumex and Automechanika
- Operate a customer-centric model aimed at becoming a dependable partner in the customer's manufacturing or project journey rather than a seller of profiles

outlook.body: The Company operates an integrated manufacturing facility at Kharagpur with an installed extrusion capacity of 15,000 MTPA, described as providing the flexibility and precision to serve diverse customer needs. A brownfield expansion at the same Kharagpur site is ongoing and is expected to add 9,000 MT of capacity; management describes it as central to the Company's future agenda, aimed not only at adding tonnage but at strengthening manufacturing flexibility, service capability and readiness to serve more specialised applications in the next phase of demand. No commissioning date, ramp schedule or rupee project cost is stated in the routed text. Funding-side, the Board approved raising up to Rs. 45 Crores by way of a Rights Issue (Draft Letter of Offer filed with the Stock Exchange on 24th April 2026, in-principle approval pending), and the Company retained the entire FY 2025-26 profits in the business, recommending no dividend, in view of its capital requirement and growth.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's aluminium demand is projected to rise meaningfully over the coming years, with the extrusion market expected to benefit from infrastructure development, renewable energy expansion, transport modernisation and the shift toward higher-value engineered applications
- Growth in infrastructure, power transmission, renewable energy, transportation and advanced manufacturing is steadily widening the application base for aluminium solutions
- Global aluminium consumption including primary and recycled metal rose to about 104 million tonnes, up 3.2% year on year, with transportation at 28% of demand, building and construction 22%, packaging 16% and electrical and electronics 15%
- The global aluminium market moved into a supply deficit estimated at around 400,000 tonnes - 600,000 tonnes in 2025, while prices strengthened amid tariff changes and sourcing pressures
- Global extrusion consumption reached approximately 35.25 million tonnes in calendar year 2025 and is projected to rise to about 36.14 million tonnes in 2026
- Demand mix is gradually moving from standard profiles to more advanced and engineered solutions where precision, performance, finish quality and technical consistency matter far more
- India shows a demand-supply gap of nearly 1.3 million tonnes - primary aluminium production in FY 2025-26 projected at approximately 4.65 million tonnes against total consumption estimated around 5.95 million tonnes
- Domestic extrusion consumption reached about 11.2 lakh tonnes in FY 2025-26, growing around 8.4% year on year, with building and construction at 48.5%, transportation including EVs 19.2%, electrical and electronics 12.8%, machinery and equipment 9.1% and consumer durables 5.9% - described by management as broad-based and diversified rather than single-sector growth
- Margin/earnings levers cited are sharper procurement practices, disciplined energy management and stronger production planning rather than volume growth - production was deliberately kept largely stable at 13,325 MT versus 13,433 MT
- Raw material prices, energy costs and market demand fluctuations are cited as the industry variables the Company must balance against growth and profitability

Funding-side, the Board approved raising up to Rs. 45 Crores by way of a Rights Issue (Draft Letter of Offer filed with the Stock Exchange on 24th April 2026, in-principle approval pending), and the Company retained the entire FY 2025-26 profits in the business, recommending no dividend, in view of its capital requirement and growth.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated manufacturing facility at Kharagpur with 15,000 MTPA installed extrusion capacity, described as providing flexibility and precision to serve diverse customer needs
- Long-standing customer relationships sustained by the ability to understand customer requirements and translate them into reliable engineering solutions, not product quality alone
- Qualification for demanding, high-value applications - supplies for ISRO's Gaganyaan programme and new automotive applications
- Operating discipline reflected in improved returns: Return on Capital Employed improved to 17.24% from 16.54%, with Current Ratio at 1.36 and Debt-Equity Ratio at 0.75
- Diversified end-market exposure across infrastructure, electrical, transportation, defence, engineering, packaging, irrigation and marine

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Improve operational efficiency, increase the share of value-added products and deepen engagement with high-value applications
- Make the Kharagpur brownfield expansion central to the forward agenda - not only adding tonnage but enhancing readiness for the next phase of demand and enabling faster response and more specialised applications
- Strengthen the capital base and financial flexibility through a proposed Rights Issue of up to Rs. 45 crore to support long-term growth plans
- Modernise the manufacturing ecosystem through technology - implementation of SAP HANA during the year, plus better …
